headline: Creates a federal committee to monitor and enforce the labor rules in the US-Mexico-Canada trade agreement (USMCA).
what_it_does: This order sets up the Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement, as called for by Section 711 of the law that put the USMCA trade deal into effect. The committee brings together several federal agencies. Its job is to keep track of whether the labor commitments in the agreement are being followed and to support enforcement of them. Details beyond the title were not provided.

who_it_affects.how: Officials from these agencies will serve on a shared committee that monitors labor rules under the USMCA.

who_it_affects.group: Workers in Mexico, Canada, and the US in industries covered by USMCA trade
who_it_affects.how: Their working conditions are the focus of the labor commitments the committee is set up to monitor.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that trade goods across the US, Mexico, and Canada borders
who_it_affects.how: They could be affected if the committee's monitoring leads to enforcement actions over labor rules.
